title: The robot loop
summary: readInputs, your code, writeOutputs: every 20 ms.

say.never: Every 20 thousandths of a second your robot does the same three things, over and over: **read** the sensors, **think** (that's your code), then **send orders** to the motors. The robot library does this loop for you, so you never call `readInputs` or `writeOutputs` yourself.
say.bit: MWLib runs this loop for you. You never call readInputs or writeOutputs yourself.

board.code:
every 20 ms:
  1. readInputs()    // motors report position and velocity
  2. your code       // robotPeriodic(), teleopPeriodic() say what you WANT
  3. writeOutputs()  // the request goes to the motors

say.never: Why three separate steps? Because your code then always works with fresh, up-to-date readings, and it only has to say what it *wants*, like "go forward half speed". The library delivers that to the motors. Big robots use this idea for every mechanism.
say.bit: Your code only ever works with fresh readings and only says what it wants. That's an **IO model**, and every mechanism on the competition robot works this way.
